content:
I have a question for you. I have always thought that “OO前夜” means “the eve of something”, basically equal to 前夕. For example 聖誕前夜 (Christmas eve). So 忘卻前夜 means “the eve of forgetting / before nigh before we forget”. I have never thought of 前夜 being the object of “being forgotten”, which makes it “to forget the last night”.

Why did you interpret it that way?
